name: geothermal-conductivity-assumptions
title: Franzmann lithology-to-thermal-conductivity assumptions
description: Original Excel workbook mapping GLiM's 16 rock classes to conductivity in W/(m K). The first worksheet contains the coefficients actually applied; the second preserves the reference table. Water-body conductivity was changed from 0.6 to 2.5 W/(m K) because of interpolation problems. No-data cells also receive 2.5 W/(m K). Preserved without editing the workbook.

sources.title: GLiM class codes and names, Hartmann and Moosdorf (2012), Table A2
Coefficient table, Aghahosseini and Breyer (2020), From hot rock to useful energy, Table 1; the second worksheet reproduces all 16 classes and values

Method described in Franzmann et al. (2025), section 2.3; its citation of the coefficients as reference [27], a 2018 compressed-air storage paper, appears to mean reference [12], Aghahosseini and Breyer (2020)

ethos:derivation: David Franzmann combined GLiM class identifiers with the conductivity coefficients of Aghahosseini and Breyer (2020), Table 1, and changed the water-body coefficient from 0.6 to the default 2.5 W/(m K). Used by map_litho_to_therm_conduct.py and now by reskit.geothermal.preprocessing.create_geothermal_resource. This workbook is a local modeling input, not a thermal-conductivity product from PANGAEA.

ethos:attribution: Franzmann, David (2022): lithology-to-thermal-conductivity assumptions (Mapper_Lithologic_to_heat_conductivity.xlsx). Forschungszentrum Julich, Institute of Climate and Energy Systems (ICE-2). Released under CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. Workbook reproduced unedited. The conductivity coefficients are from Aghahosseini, Arman and Breyer, Christian (2020): From hot rock to useful energy: A global estimate of enhanced geothermal systems potential. Applied Energy 279, 115769, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apenergy.2020.115769, Table 1 -- cite that paper for the coefficients themselves. The rock classes they are keyed to are from Hartmann, Jens and Moosdorf, Nils (2012): The new global lithological map database GLiM. https://doi.org/10.1029/2012GC004370, Table A2.
ethos:provenance: Copied unchanged from Franzmann's restored dissertation archive on 2026-09-09. The first worksheet's mapping reproduces the archived 0.5-degree conductivity raster exactly. The second worksheet matches Aghahosseini and Breyer (2020), Table 1, value for value; SOURCE-EXCERPTS.md quotes the relevant passages of all three sources. The paper describes the mapping approach but does not specify the water-body override or raster nodata handling.
